newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Red Cross hostages to be released in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross hostages to be released in Tajikistan.

text.p: The head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in Tajikistan said on Friday two of its employees held hostage by rebels in the former Soviet republic were being released.

"I have just spoken to (rebel) commander Bakhrom and he has announced the two ICRC representatives are being released at this very moment," Thomas Merkelbach, head of the ICRC mission in the war-ravaged country, told a news conference in Dushanbe. "They are being released without preconditions," he said.

The Red Cross hostages freed are British national Elizabeth Trinch and her Tajik translator. The Red Cross suspended operations after four employees with the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR), including a Nigerian national, were kidnapped by the group in the capital Dushanbe on Thursday.
The UNHCR workers, four U.N. military observers -- from Austria, Switzerland and Ukraine -- and four Russian journalists were still being held by the group, a U.N. spokesman said.

The hostage-takers are part of a group commanded by Rizvon Sadirov, who used to fight for the Islamic opposition but whose loyalties are now unclear. They are demanding free passage for other group members to return from neighbouring Afghanistan.

Tajikistan, a mountainous country bordering China, has been racked by a bitter four-year civil war but a ceasefire agreed between the government and the armed Islamic opposition last December appears to be holding. The government has pledged to negotiate the hostages' release.
